video_title: 🟢 LIVE : Will crypto get clarity? Senate votes today
transcript: Good morning, everyone. We are live. It's Tuesday, September 15th, and in 4 hours, the Senate votes on whether to take up the Clarity Act, which is the bill that decides who regulates crypto in the United States. Um with me is Summer Mersinger, CEO of the Blockchain Association, and Kevin Wysocki, Head of Policy at Anchorage Digital. Um so, very excited to have this conversation today, just hours before the vote. Um before we get going, I want to thank Oasis, which is supporting the stream. Oasis is a self-custody wallet with no single point of failure. It has a two of three multi-sig. You hold two keys, they hold a recovery key. So, it's easier to recover your assets if anything happens, and right now they are raffling a CryptoPunk. So, the first 500 people who start a plan in September or October get a chance to win the punk. So, check that out at oasisvault.io/cryptopunk. Okay, so, um let's get to talking at Clarity. Yesterday, Republican senators presented a new draft bill that addressed key issues, especially on ethics. Um it um it it made a supposedly a an ethics draft that President Trump agreed to, uh and overnight the Democrats apparently sent a counter-proposal. Um odds of the bill of the culture vote passing today went down overnight because we haven't heard back from Democrats on whether they'll actually [snorts] um agree to the new draft version. Uh but, much better than me to tell you about all these things, Summer and Kevin. So, uh to just kind of get us up to speed or of where we stand today, it's been many months, countless calls and meetings. Um I know kind of the crypto lobby has been pounding the pavement in DC trying to get this passed. It must be exhausting and today we get kind of the clear the clearest sign of whether the bill can pass uh this year or whether it gets postponed. So, uh maybe somewhere let's start with you. Um a lot of the rhetoric you see publicly is is pretty typical um when Congre- or when the Senate is debating these, you know, it's kind of a live debate. So, of course they're going to take pretty extreme positions publicly where they're actually having productive conversations. They've had productive conversation. There's been so much staff time and effort, senator level time and effort put into this bill that really tells me there is a um desire to get to yes from um both sides. So, I actually am feeling pretty good about today's vote. Um you know, I will say that crypto certainly didn't get everything we wanted in this bill and there were places in this bill that we, you know, feel like we've had to really compromise further than um you know, we expected to. But there's, you know, we recognize that this is the moment that we need to get durable legislation, get laws in the on the books. And you know, what I've kind of tried to impress upon those who are kind of in the in the last negotiation, you know, minute negotiations here is you've got to stop and ask yourself is is the status quo going to be an okay outcome? So, my hope is that again, a lot of the rhetoric we're seeing is just that rhetoric, and that, you know, these senators really are working to get to yes today. >> What do you think, Kevin? Are you as optimistic as Summer? >> I definitely think it's a historic moment ushering this next wave of financial innovation, right? Tokenization, stablecoin infrastructure, uh tokenized deposits, all these wonderful things that are already happening and only will be spurred further with the enactment of the Clarity Act. Um we've had a lot of good conversations, obviously, with key Senate offices on this. There's been tremendous progress on matters like ethics, on stablecoin rewards, on uh the BRCA, right? The developer protections provision. Um we've we've recently heard that the Republicans are not going to take up the counter proposal from the Democrats. Um and it we're going to continue to have this vote at 2:15 last I heard. So, I think you're going to probably see a couple of Democrats support this. Um I think you're going to have most of the Republicans, and I'm hoping with in the next couple of hours we can get a few more of these senators that we need over the fence to yes. Um there's been so much um that we've done in the last like 48 hours to get here.
